content:
Mensuration pays double for care. The formulas are short — trapezium, rhombus, cylinder. The marks are lost in units. Mix cm with m once, and a perfect set-up scores zero. Take the free IMO Class 8 Mensuration online test below before any revision. Ten MCQs, instant score, full explanations — it will tell you exactly what to fix first.

What the IMO asks from Mensuration in Class 8

  • Areas: trapezium, rhombus, and a quadrilateral split by a diagonal.
  • Composite figures — fields, windows, borders and paths.
  • Surface areas: cubes, cuboids, cylinders, painted walls, open boxes.
  • Volumes and capacity in litres.
  • Melt-and-recast and water-displacement classics.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Trapezium area = ½(a + b) × h. Rhombus area = ½ d₁d₂.
  • Cylinder: CSA = 2πrh and volume = πr²h. With π = 22/7, radii in 7s cancel fast.
  • 1 m³ = 1000 litres. 1 litre = 1000 cm³. Capacity sums live on these two lines.
  • Melting keeps the VOLUME. Recast metal keeps its volume, never its surface area.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Using the slant side of a trapezium as its height.
  • Finding TSA when the question wants only the walls.
  • Forgetting that an open box is missing exactly one face.

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Mensuration Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A rhombus has area 120 cm². If one of its diagonals is 15 cm, what is the length of the other diagonal?
questions.explanation: Area = 1/2 x d1 x d2. So 120 = 1/2 × 15 x d2. This gives d2 = 240/15 = 16 cm.

questions.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 10 cm. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Half-diagonals are 12 cm and 5 cm. Side = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √(169) = 13 cm. Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52 cm.

questions.q: A trapezium ABCD has parallel sides AB = 25 cm and DC = 11 cm. The non-parallel sides AD = 13 cm and BC = 15 cm. Find the area of the trapezium.
questions.explanation: Drop perpendiculars from D and C onto AB. Let the foot from D be at distance a from A. Then AD² = a² + h² gives 169 = a² + h². The foot from C is at distance (a + 11) from A, so (25 - a - 11)² + h² = BC² gives (14 - a)²

questions.q: Rhombus-shaped tiles, each with diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm, are used to cover a rectangular floor of dimensions 48 cm by 36 cm. How many tiles are needed?
questions.explanation: Area of floor = 48 × 36 = 1728 cm². Area of each tile = 1/2 × 6 x 8 = 24 cm². Number of tiles = 1728/24 = 72.

questions.q: Find the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 15 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: CSA of cylinder = 2 x pi x r x h = 2 × 22/7 × 7 x 15 = 44 × 15 = 660 cm².

questions.q: Two identical cubes of edge 5 cm are joined face-to-face to form a cuboid. Find the total surface area of the resulting cuboid.
questions.explanation: When two cubes of edge 5 are joined, the resulting cuboid is 10 × 5 x 5. TSA = 2(10x5 + 5x5 + 10x5) = 2(50 + 25 + 50) = 2 × 125 = 250 cm². Alternatively: total TSA of both cubes = 2 × 6 x 25 = 300. Joining removes two 5

questions.q: A cube of edge 6 cm is placed centrally on top of a cuboid of dimensions 6 cm x 6 cm x 10 cm. Find the total surface area of the combined solid.
questions.explanation: The cube sits perfectly on the cuboid since both have 6 × 6 top/bottom faces. The combined solid is effectively a cuboid of 6 × 6 x 16. TSA = 2(6x6 + 6x16 + 6x16) = 2(36 + 96 + 96) = 2 × 228 = 456 cm². Alternatively: TSA

questions.q: The volume of a cube is 1331 cm³. Find the edge of the cube.
questions.explanation: Edge = cube root of 1331 = 11 cm, since 11 × 11 × 11 = 1331.

questions.q: A cuboid has its length twice its breadth and its breadth twice its height. If the volume is 512 cm³, find the height.
questions.explanation: Let height = h. Then breadth = 2h and length = 4h. Volume = 4h x 2h x h = 8h³. So 8h³ = 512, giving h³ = 64 and h = 4 cm.

questions.q: Which holds more water and by how much: a cubical container of edge 11 cm, or a cylindrical container of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Volume of cube = 11³ = 1331 cm³. Volume of cylinder = 22/7 × 7² x 7 = 22 × 49 = 1078 cm³. The cube holds more by 1331 - 1078 = 253 cm³.
